answer.rationale: With expiry in 14 days, no auto-renew, and the line at 94% of committed volume, switching primary supply or deferring creates avoidable delivery risk; adding a second source is valuable but likely slower than the single available decision and may not meet the 18% in-year mandate alone. Negotiating renewal terms with the incumbent is the lowest-risk path to near-term TCO reduction: prior renewal preserved stability, benchmarking moved price and payment terms, and longer commitments unlocked volume pricing without narrowing service scope. I am verifying the two memories most central to whether negotiation can realistically produce the required cut before expiry.
